patterns: APPSC asks drain of wealth as direct single facts: 'popularised by' Naoroji, drain reason = profits of British capitalists, drain associated with British (not Portuguese/French/Dutch).
Strong AP tilt: textiles as second-largest employer after agriculture in Andhra, Visakhapatnam manganese world leader 1892-1929, Guntur/Kurnool famines.
UPSC/other PSCs ask Home Charges components, imperial preference, Industrial Revolution ruining handicrafts, commercialisation of agriculture, opium triangular trade, Hilton Young ratio.
Recurring dates: first cotton mill Bombay 1854, Assam Company 1839, Punjab Land Alienation Act 1900, Famine Code 1883.
App MCQs use many multi-statement and A-R items on famine commissions, Andhra textile places and eve-of-independence indicators - more detail than APPSC's single-fact asks.
